message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several key rights under state law and local ordinances. Here’s a quick overview: | Category | What You’re Entitled To | |----------|------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlords may charge up to one month’s rent (or two if the lease is longer than 12 months).
• Must be returned within 30 days after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the property safe, clean, and in good repair.
• Must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical, and structural integrity. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must give reasonable notice (usually 24–48 hours) before entering your unit, except in emergencies. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease; late fees are allowed but must be disclosed in writing. | | **Lease Terms** | • Written lease required for rentals over 30 days.
• Lease can’t contain illegal clauses (e.g., waiving your right to sue). | | **Discrimination** | • Fair Housing Act protects against discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, family status, etc. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must follow the court process; no “self‑help” evictions.
• Notice periods vary (e.g., 30 days for nonpayment, 60 days for lease termination). | | **Repair & Deduct** | • If landlord fails to fix major problems, you may repair and deduct from rent (but only after giving written notice). | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • You’re entitled to live without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | For detailed guidance tailored to your situation—like how to handle a security deposit dispute or what to do if your landlord refuses to make repairs—consider consulting a local attorney or tenant advocacy group.
